chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
water is a solution. Again, $15\text{ gram}$ salt in $250\text{ gram}$ water is also a solution. The one with lesser amount of salt is a dilute solution while the other is a concentrated solution. Again, $10\text{ gram}$ salt is mixed in two glasses containing $250\text{ mL}$ and $200\text{ mL}$ water each. The solution containing more water is a dilute solution while the one with less water is a concentrated solution. Similarly in the laboratory, smaller amounts of solute in a fixed amount of solvent creates a dilute solution and greater amounts of solute in the same amount of solvent creates a concentrated solution. Actually, there is no specific rule to determine which is dilute and which is a concentrated solution.

The number of moles dissolved in every liter of solution at a certain temperature is called the molarity of the solution. If $2\text{ mole}$ solute is dissolved in a one liter solution at a fixed temperature, then the molarity of that solution is $2$. When there is $0.5\text{ mole}$ solute in $1\text{ liter}$ solution, that is a semi-molar solution and when that same $1\text{ liter}$ solution has $0.1\text{ mole}$ solute, that is called a decimolar solution. The molarity of a decimolar solution is $0.1$ while $0.5$ is the molarity of a semimolar solution.

sections.section_title: Preparation of Solutions with Different Molarity
sections.content_markdown:
There is necessity of preparing molar, semimolar and decimolar solutions in the laboratory. It can be done easily following various steps. Firstly, you need to select a volumetric flask. Secondly, you need to weigh the substance that you are interested to prepare the solution of and put it in the flask. Thirdly, you need to add some water and shake the flask to prepare the solution. Then, you need to fill water to a certain mark in the flask. There is relationship in between molarity of solution, volume of solution, mass and molecular mass of the solute.

$$\text{Mass of solute in gram unit} = \frac{\text{molarity of solution} \times \text{volume of solution in mililiter unit} \times \text{molecular mass}}{1000}$$

Here, if we take $\text{Mass of solute in gram unit} = w$
$$\text{Molarity of solution} = S$$
$$\text{volume of solution in mililiter unit} = V$$
